text.title: Agency Revenue Mix Audit Template Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules governing how an agency's trailing-12-month revenue is measured, split by type, and turned into dependence flags: the net-revenue base, the isolation of owner-billed work, concentration thresholds on both clients and referral partners, and what may legitimately be called a retainer.

rule.statement: All percentages in `revenue_by_type` MUST be computed on net revenue (gross income): media spend, ad buys, print, licences and subcontractor cost that are rebilled at or near cost are reported as a separate `pass_through` line and excluded from the denominator.

rationale.source: Agency M&A practice — net revenue / gross income convention

rule.rationale: Billings-based mix makes a media-heavy agency look large and diversified while contribution is flat. Buyers restate to net revenue in the first week of diligence; the mix percentages move materially and every conclusion drawn from the billings version is withdrawn.

rule.statement: Revenue delivered personally by the owner MUST be its own `owner_billed` line with the underlying delivery hours, never folded into `project` or `retainer`. Record it even when the owner takes no salary for that work.

rationale.source: M&A quality-of-earnings — owner add-backs and replacement cost

rule.rationale: Owner-delivered work does not transfer at close. The buyer must hire a producer to replace it, so the replacement salary is subtracted from EBITDA. Hiding the line inside `project` overstates transferable earnings by exactly the replacement cost, and the correction lands as a price re-trade.

rule.statement: The audit MUST flag any single client at 20% or more of trailing-12-month net revenue, and any top-3 clients at 50% or more combined, each as an entry in `dependence_risks` with a named mitigation.

rationale.source: Lower-middle-market M&A and lender diligence — customer concentration

rule.rationale: At those levels the loss of one account removes the buyer's debt service, not just its margin. Lenders respond by requiring escrow, an earnout or a seller note, which converts headline price into contingent price — the concentration is repriced as deal structure rather than as multiple.

rule.statement: Channel concentration MUST be measured alongside client concentration: flag any single referral partner, marketplace or platform that originated 25% or more of new revenue in the window.

rationale.source: Revenue-concentration analysis — origination vs billing view

rule.rationale: A referral partner is a single point of failure that is invisible in a client-level table, because the risk sits one level upstream: the client roster looks diversified while every one of those logos arrived through one relationship that can be withdrawn in a single conversation.

rule.statement: The window is a rolling 12 months of revenue recognized by service delivery date. Cash receipts, issued invoices, deposits and annual prepayments MUST be allocated across the delivery period, not booked in the month of receipt.

rationale.source: ASC 606 / IFRS 15 — revenue recognized as performance obligations are satisfied

rule.rationale: A December prepay or a large project deposit booked on cash inflates the retainer share and creates a recurring line that does not exist. The mix then shows rising predictability in exactly the period where the agency actually pulled cash forward.

rule.statement: A line may be classified `retainer` only if a written agreement exists with a stated term and a notice period of 30 days or more. Ongoing month-to-month work cancellable at will is classified `project`, however long it has been running.
rule.rationale: Buyers read the contracts and reprice zero-notice "retainers" to project multiples, because revenue that can stop next month carries the same risk as revenue that has to be re-won next month. Misclassification here is the most common single cause of a diligence-stage re-trade in agency deals.

rule.statement: Each entry in `multiplier_impact` MUST name the mix share it responds to, the direction of the effect, and the mechanism (transferability, predictability, or margin). Bare numeric multiplier deltas with no named driver are rejected.
rule.rationale: A delta with no driver cannot be acted on: the founder cannot tell whether to convert project work into retainers, to reduce owner-billed hours, or to drop a low-margin service line. Naming the mechanism turns the audit into a work plan instead of a score.
